title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The delete method unconditionally deletes the requester's 'me' snooze (my_snooze.delete() at line 180) for the user without any authorization check, unlike the shared 'everyone' snooze which is guarded by can_edit_alert_rule(project.organization, request). Although ProjectAlertRulePermission enforces a project scope, can_edit_alert_rule also performs an organization-membership check (OrganizationMember exists for the user) for user tokens; the self-snooze deletion path bypasses that check, so a request with only a project scope (and no organization membership) could delete a RuleSnooze owned by a different user if it could enumerate that user's snooze, or at minimum a missing authorization check is applied to a protected operation. This is a newly reachable code path because the PR refactored rule resolution into convert_args and changed the delete signature from (project, rule_id) to (project, rule).

findings.suggested_fix: Guard the my_snooze deletion with the same authorization check used for shared snoozes (e.g., `if my_snooze and can_edit_alert_rule(project.organization, request):`), or require organization membership / target=='me' validation before deleting a user-owned snooze. Alternatively, verify that `request.user` is the owner of the snooze being deleted (owner_id == request.user.id or user_id == request.user.id) before performing my_snooze.delete().
